comment.base: Nicolás Maduro Moros, often referred to simply as Maduro, is a Venezuelan politician born on November 23, 1962, in Caracas. He started his career as a bus driver for the Caracas Metro system and became a prominent trade union leader. In the 1990s, he aligned himself with Hugo Chávez’s socialist movement, the Fifth Republic Movement, after Chávez’s release from prison following a failed 1992 coup attempt. Maduro’s political ascent began in earnest after Chávez won the presidency in 1998: Maduro was elected to Venezuela’s National Constituent Assembly in 1999, then to the National Assembly in 2000, where he served as speaker from 2005 to 2006. He later became foreign minister under Chávez from 2006 to 2013 and vice president from 2012 onward. Following Chávez’s death from cancer on March 5, 2013, Maduro assumed the role of interim president and narrowly won a special election in April 2013 against opposition leader Henrique Capriles, securing his first full term. He was re-elected in 2018 amid widespread allegations of fraud and boycotts by the opposition, and again in 2024 in a highly disputed vote where the opposition claimed victory based on tally sheets but Maduro refused to release detailed results, leading to international condemnation and domestic unrest. Maduro has faced longstanding accusations from the U.S. and international bodies. In March 2020, the U.S. Department of Justice indicted him on charges of narco-terrorism conspiracy (for allegedly partnering with Colombian FARC rebels to flood the U.S. with cocaine), conspiracy to import cocaine, possession of machine guns and destructive devices, and related weapons offenses. These stem from claims that he led the “Cartel of the Suns,” a drug-trafficking network involving Venezuelan military and government officials. Additionally, the International Criminal Court has investigated him for crimes against humanity, including arbitrary detentions, torture, extrajudicial killings, and suppression of dissent during protests.
